title: Mastering the FTC Engineering Portfolio
description: Learn how to build a compelling engineering portfolio for FIRST Tech Challenge competitions. This workshop covers documentation best practices, design process explanation, and presentation techniques that impress judges.
content:
About This Workshop

Building a great engineering portfolio can be the difference between standing out or blending in at competitions. In this session, you'll learn exactly what judges are looking for and how to present your work in the most compelling way.

What You'll Learn

  • How to structure your engineering notebook
  • Best practices for design process documentation
  • Common mistakes teams make and how to avoid them
  • Tips for presenting your robot's design to judges

Who Should Attend

Any FTC team member — builders, programmers, or team leads — who wants to improve their competition documentation and presentation skills.

title: MechGirl CAD Challenge 2026
description: Annual CAD design challenge with the theme 'Robots for Community Support'. Participants will design a robot that solves a real-world community problem. Prizes for top 3 designs.
content:
About The Challenge

Our annual CAD design challenge is back! This year, the theme is Robots for Community Support. We want you to design a robot that solves a real-world problem in your community — whether it's helping at a local food bank, assisting in a community garden, or supporting an elderly neighbor.

Challenge Timeline

  • Registration opens: August 1, 2026
  • Submission deadline: October 1, 2026
  • Winners announced: October 15, 2026

Prizes

  • 1st Place: $500 + 3D printing kit
  • 2nd Place: $250 + CAD software license
  • 3rd Place: $100 + engineering book bundle

Requirements

Submissions must include a 3D CAD model (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, or Onshape), a technical drawing, and a brief design rationale document.

title: Introduction to Robot Kinematics
description: A beginner-friendly workshop on robot kinematics. Learn about forward kinematics, inverse kinematics, and how to implement them in your robotics projects using Python and MATLAB.
content:
What is Robot Kinematics?

Kinematics is the study of motion without considering the forces that cause it. In robotics, this means understanding how a robot's joints and links move to achieve desired positions and orientations.

Workshop Topics

  • Forward kinematics: determining end-effector position from joint angles
  • Inverse kinematics: calculating joint angles for a desired position
  • Workspace analysis and joint limits
  • Implementing kinematics in Python with NumPy
  • Visualization using MATLAB and Python

Prerequisites

Basic knowledge of trigonometry and some programming experience in Python is recommended. No prior robotics experience needed!

Software Setup

Participants will receive installation instructions for Python (with NumPy and Matplotlib) and MATLAB a week before the workshop.

title: 3D Printing for Mechanical Design
description: Hands-on masterclass covering parametric modeling, print preparation, material selection, and post-processing techniques for functional mechanical parts.
content:
About This Masterclass

A comprehensive hands-on session covering the entire 3D printing workflow for mechanical design. From parametric modeling to post-processing, you'll leave with the skills to print functional parts for your robotics projects.

Topics Covered

  • Parametric modeling techniques in Fusion 360
  • Design for additive manufacturing (DfAM)
  • Print orientation and support strategies
  • Material selection: PLA, PETG, ABS, and nylon
  • Calibration and troubleshooting
  • Post-processing: sanding, painting, and acetone smoothing

Hands-On Projects

Each participant will design and print a custom gear reduction housing during the session. Bring your laptop with Fusion 360 installed (free for students).

Location

MakerSpace Lab — materials and printers will be provided. Safety equipment available on-site.

title: Women in STEM Panel Discussion
description: Join industry professionals and researchers sharing their journeys in mechanical engineering and robotics. Q&A session included. Network with like-minded peers.
content:
About The Panel

Five accomplished women from different corners of mechanical engineering and robotics will share their stories, challenges, and advice. From industry engineers to academic researchers, this panel represents the diversity of paths available in STEM.

Panelists

  • Dr. Sarah Chen — Robotics Engineer at Boston Dynamics
  • Maria Lopez — Lead Mechanical Engineer, NASA JPL
  • Priya Sharma — Founder & CEO, RoboEd Labs
  • Dr. Aisha Johnson — Associate Professor, MIT Mechanical Engineering
  • Emma Williams — Automation Engineer, Tesla

What to Expect

  • Honest conversations about navigating a career in STEM
  • Advice for students and early-career engineers
  • Open Q&A — submit questions in advance or ask live
  • Networking session after the panel discussion

Who Can Attend

This event is open to everyone — students, professionals, parents, and educators. Bring a friend!
